title: Encapsulation, Constructors and static
summary: Access modifiers and why fields should be private, getters and setters with validation, constructor overloading and this(...), immutable classes with final fields, static fields and methods, static factory methods, constants, and when a class should be a utility class.

So only the class's own methods can change them and keep the object valid

Callers then have to go through methods like `deposit`, which can refuse nonsense values. Subclasses cannot see private fields either.

No: a static method runs without any object

A static method belongs to the class, so it has no `this`; it can use only static fields, other static methods and its parameters.

cards.q: A class has `private static int count = 0;` and its constructor does `count++`. After creating 3 objects, what is `count`?
cards.a:
3, shared by all objects

A static field is a single variable shared by the whole class, so every constructor call adds to the same one.
